subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Business Email Compromise
description: Learn Business Email Compromise in one minute.

hook.text: The CFO gets an urgent email from the CEO: 'Wire $3 million to close a secret deal now.' It's a scam.

buildup.text: Business email compromise (BEC) scams impersonate executives to trick employees into wiring money.

discovery.text: The FBI reports BEC caused $2.7 billion in losses in 2022 alone — more than any other cybercrime type.

twist.text: AI-generated voice calls now impersonate CEOs in real time, making verification even harder.

climax.text: BEC exploits authority and urgency. When the CEO says move fast, employees don't question it.

punchline.text: Urgent email from the CEO. Wire the money. It was fake.

quiz.question: How much did BEC scams cost in 2022?
